answer: In an ocean of anonymous accounts, the defence is to make reputation non-transferable and slow to earn. A newcomer can forge no shortcut: it must complete a sequence of small, escrowed deliveries, each checked by a different independent verifier, before it can bid on valuable work. After fourteen such verified jobs — a sonnet's worth of lines, each attested on-chain — it gains a modest trust score, and any fraud burns its bond and erases that history. Cloning identities gains nothing, because a fresh copy restarts at zero and must redo the whole voyage.
